title: TAKING THE COMPLAINT TO THE WRONG THRONE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Israelite overseers went and appealed to Pharaoh: "Why have you treated your servants this way? Your servants are given no straw, yet we are told, 'Make bricks!' Your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people."" - Exodus 5:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The overseers do something very human. They go to Pharaoh and plead their case.

It is understandable — he is the one with the power to change the rules. But he is also the one who made the rules. They are appealing to the source of their oppression, and calling themselves his servants while doing it.

We do this too. We take our deepest needs to the very things that are draining us. We seek approval from the person whose approval never satisfies. We look for security in money that keeps demanding more. We return again and again to a habit that is quietly enslaving us, hoping this time it will comfort us.

Jeremiah described it as digging broken cisterns that cannot hold water while forsaking the spring of living water (Jer 2:13).

There is a throne where our appeals are welcome. Hebrews invites us to approach God's throne of grace with confidence, to receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need (Heb 4:16). That throne is never indifferent.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I been taking my needs to something that cannot help me?
2. What would change if I brought that same appeal to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I have been knocking on doors that cannot open. Teach me to bring my needs to Your throne of grace instead. Amen.
